correctness.rationale: The complete primary paper was read, including Definition 2.2 and Proposition 4.4. For t >= 1 the latter reduces the finite-dimensional supremum to extreme points. In the cube, a signed-permutation normalization gives x=(1,a_2,...,a_n) with a_2=s_2(x); every sign vertex has shifted norms bounded by the unordered pair {2,1+a_2}, and the vertex (1,-1,1,...,1) attains that pair. Monotonicity of the power mean proves the exact formula. Boundary cases a_2=0 and a_2=1 are included. No finite experiment is used as the proof.
risks: The theorem is limited to finite-dimensional real ell-infinity spaces and finite t >= 1; no extension outside that domain is inferred.

value.rationale: The result computes a complete pointwise profile on a canonical non-strictly-convex Banach space, identifies the exact coordinate statistic controlling it, gives all extremal loci, and clarifies the natural p=infinity endpoint of the known finite-p pointwise-constancy threshold. This is a structural family formula rather than a routine single-value recomputation.
risks: The result is elementary once the correct extreme-point reduction and coordinate statistic are identified; its value rests on completeness of the profile and the endpoint phenomenon, not on proof complexity.
